name: K-Rab
sources: Stereogum — The Number Ones: D4L's "Laffy Taffy": https://stereogum.com/2209651/the-number-ones-d4ls-laffy-taffy/columns/the-number-ones
Complex — Fabo on D4L's "Laffy Taffy" ten years on: https://www.complex.com/music/a/lauren-nostro/fabo-d4l-laffy-taffy-10-year-anniversary
notes: The most extreme minimalism on the axis, and the research gives its design goal in the producer's own words: "for a song to sound good as a ringtone, it had to be synthy and minimal. It had to sound cheap." Every parameter here is that sentence. `melody.register` is [78, 98] and `densityPerBar` is [1, 3] — the sparsest lead in the batch — with `contour.riff` 0.97, `phraseBars` weighted 8:1 to a single bar, and `emptyBarBias` 0.28. `percs` is one snap lane at a fixed one hit a bar. `chords` is a `i` at weight 9 with `extensions.triad` 0.99 — there is no colour in this record at all. ⛔ **The motif is two notes and it is authored as [2, 3], one wider than the record.** The research is unambiguous that it is a two-note figure transcribed from the producer's toddler; the third pitch is the concession the melodic-variety floor requires, since a part still owes a producer 55 distinct outputs over 200 seeds, and it is weighted out of the way by `intervals` rather than being pretended into the description. ⚠ **The hats are the research's "optional or absent" and 0.28 is the floor.** A model that declares a hat block owes every seed a hat, so `fillDensity` cannot go below 0.28 no matter what the record does; `base` weights the 8th 4:2 over the 16th, which is the rest of what "absent" can honestly mean here. ⛔ **The fill is wrong in kind and it is an engine limit, not a reading.** "808 drumrolls" are the only fill this producer uses, and the fill generator writes a snare roll with no route onto the 808 — `gapProb` 0.52 keeps what fires broken rather than letting a snare stream stand in for a tom roll. ⚠ **Confidence is medium against the research's high-medium**, and the inferred parameter is the tempo: the 70–80 half-time band is marked [LOW-CONF on the number], so 140–160 is a lane reading. The origin of the motif, the kit and the design logic are what is sourced. ⚠ Total simultaneous parts are 3 by the research's count, which `arrangement.sectionRules` honours by naming three in the hook and never adding a fourth. ⚠ **A register here spanned less than an octave and has been widened.** The 808 places its root with `pitch_class_in_register`, which returns nothing — and therefore writes NO 808 at all — when the window holds no octave of the key it was asked for. An eleven-semitone window misses one pitch class entirely, so the part vanished on every seed that landed in that key. The centre of the authored range is unchanged. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 673 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 968/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 967/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.28 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 967/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
